subsystem: services/api media module + services/media-worker (error taxonomy, deletion completeness, dispatch failure)
method: Red-team integration tests against the repo's real-PostgreSQL isolated-schema harness with synthetic (clearly labeled) in-memory object store and fault-injecting queue. No held-out cases touched (wm-dink-01, afn-vic-rally1). No fabricated evidence; all counts below are from tests executed in this session.

breaks.found: Upload accepted any contentType for any kind (e.g. video/mp4 thumbnail, application/octet-stream raw_video); only a global size cap existed and thumbnails could declare up to the full video cap.
breaks.fix: Per-kind content-type allowlist and per-kind size caps in services/api/src/modules/media/routes.ts; typed 422 permanent media.unsupported_type / media.size_exceeded.

breaks.scenario: upload completion without an uploaded object
breaks.found: POST /complete trusted the client entirely: it marked assets ready without verifying the object exists in storage, so a 'ready' asset could point at nothing (corrupted_media never surfaced).
breaks.fix: Added IObjectStore.headObject; completion verifies existence and returns typed 422 corrupted_media media.object_missing.

breaks.scenario: oversized video (actual object larger than declared)
breaks.found: Declared size was checked but the actual stored object size never was; an oversized object sailed through to ready/processing.
breaks.fix: Completion compares headObject size to the per-kind cap; oversized objects are marked deleted, a purge is enqueued (asserted per-asset), and a typed 422 corrupted_media media.size_exceeded is returned.

breaks.found: A queue enqueue failure during completion left the asset stuck in 'processing' with no job on the queue and no typed error (silent stall).
breaks.fix: Typed 503 retryable media.dispatch_failed; asset reverted to 'uploading' so completion can be retried.

breaks.found: If the purge enqueue failed after DELETE committed, the object was orphaned forever: nothing ever retried it.
breaks.fix: Deletion stays committed (user intent honored), failure is logged, and a new worker sweep (sweepDeletedMedia in services/media-worker/src/worker.ts, run every runOnce) purges any deleted_at asset whose object_key is still set.

breaks.found: deletion_task rows claimed as 'processing' by a crashed worker were never re-selected (query filtered status = 'queued' only), stranding account/media purges forever.
breaks.fix: Task pickup now includes stalled 'processing' rows; regression test simulates a crash-abandoned row and proves it completes.

breaks.found: API double-delete returned 404 (acceptable typed not-found) but worker double purge re-ran deleteObject unconditionally; purge could also null object_key on a LIVE (not deleted) asset if a stray/forged purge job arrived.
breaks.fix: Purge refuses live assets (typed refusal note, object untouched), second purge is idempotent ('no object to delete'), object_key only nulled after successful storage deletion.

breaks.found: media.process did not check deleted_at: processing a deleted asset flipped its status back to 'ready' (resurrection), and a transcode finishing after deletion left orphan derived artifacts; transcoder exceptions crashed the whole worker batch (silent catch-all absent, but one poison job killed all jobs).
breaks.fix: media.process refuses deleted media, re-checks deleted_at after transcode and deletes derived artifacts produced mid-deletion, rejects derived keys outside the master prefix, marks transcode failures as status 'failed' (typed, visible), and runOnce isolates per-job failures so poison jobs return to the queue without killing the batch.

breaks.found: Purge deleted only the master object; normalized/thumbnail derivatives under the asset prefix were orphaned.
breaks.fix: deleteObjectAndDerived lists and deletes all keys under `${objectKey}/` before the master; purge without an object store leaves the job visible (unhandled) instead of faking completion, and account final_hard_delete stays queued while media_purge is blocked.

breaks.scenario: test harness races (found while red-teaming, in-subsystem test files)
breaks.found: consent.integration.test.ts and trainingConsent.test.ts did DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE and re-migrated concurrently with other suites, racing on CREATE EXTENSION/CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (reproducible duplicate-key failures); training.integration.test.ts streak test posted completions at noon UTC 'today', which is in the future before 12:00 UTC and was rejected by the server's own future-time guard.
breaks.fix: Both suites converted to the repo's isolated-schema pattern (no destructive DROP of public); streak test clamps 'today at noon UTC' to now-60s when noon is still in the future. No production behavior or assertions weakened.

invariants_verified: All error responses use the repo error envelope { error: { kind, code, message, retryable, requestId } } with kinds from the shared taxonomy (permanent, retryable, corrupted_media, ...).
Deletion is complete: master object + all derived artifacts removed; object_key nulled only after storage deletion; sweep reconciles lost purge dispatches.
Analysis of deleted media impossible: analysis dispatch (deleted_at IS NULL owner query), playback URL, upload completion, and worker media.process all refuse deleted assets; no status resurrection.
No silent catches: queue failures produce typed 503s or logged+swept states; transcoder failures mark assets failed; poison jobs remain visible on the queue; purge without storage stays unhandled.
notes: Synthetic fixtures: FakeObjectStore/FakeStore (in-memory key inventory) and FaultyQueue (single-throw enqueue) are clearly labeled synthetic in the test files. No contracts (usable-result-v1, silent-failure-v1) touched. No mobile, ML, or held-out-case changes.
